imagePrompt: Teenage boy golfer on the green, holding his own umbrella while preparing to putt in light rain.
imageAlt: Boy holding his own umbrella while putting.

issues: Umbrella position and golfer posture look slightly awkward, but still physically plausible for a self-held umbrella while addressing the ball.
imageVerification.repairPrompt: Adjust the umbrella so it looks more naturally held and balanced above the golfer's head, increasing the physical plausibility. Slightly refine the golf posture to further enhance realism for addressing a putt while holding an umbrella.

questions.title: Can someone hold an umbrella for you while you putt?
questions.question: When you are putting and it is raining, can someone else hold an umbrella over you to keep you dry?

choices.text: Yes, anyone can help by holding an umbrella while you play.
No, only you are allowed to hold your own umbrella while you take your shot.
Only your caddie can hold your umbrella for you.
You cannot use umbrellas on the golf course at all.

questions.explanation: When you take your putt, you are the only one who can hold your umbrella. No one else can cover you with an umbrella while you play your shot.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: When you are trying to hit the ball into the hole on the green using a putter.
A person who helps you by carrying your clubs and giving you advice.

questions.teachingTip: Ask kids to pretend they're holding an umbrella on the green and talk through who can hold it during their shot.
likelyMisconceptions: Some children may think it's okay for an adult or friend to hold the umbrella for them while they make a stroke.
They may believe their caddie is allowed to hold the umbrella during the shot.
